summary:
# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: THE RED RAT'S DAUGHTER (Guy Boothby, 1899, illus. Henry Austin)

### Ch I
- **John Grantham Browne** ("Browne"): 28, bachelor, cynical wit. Worth £120,000/yr (£10,000/month, £328 15s 4d/day). Ex-Eton, Christ Church.
- Father **old Brown** (no "e"): soap-maker, started as street arab in Manchester or Birmingham. Left £3.5M+ in trust. Mother: second wife, third daughter of late **Lord Rushbrooke**; died 6 months after father. Browne was 25 then.
- Yacht **Lotus Blossom** (1,200 tons), at anchor in harbour of **Merok**, **Gieranger Fjord**, Norway, 2nd week of August. Parliament up.
- Guests: **Duchess of Matlock** (wife of Sec. of State for Foreign Affairs); **Lady Iseult** and **Lady Imogen** (her daughters); **Miss Verney** (beauty of season); **Hon. Silas Dobson** (American Ambassador), wife **Mrs. Dobson**, daughter **Miss Dobson**; **George Barrington-Marsh** (1st Life Guards, "Captain Marsh"); **Jimmy Foote** (no permanent address, lives by pleasing friends); **Felix Maas** (Dutch-ish, speaks all European languages, rumoured author of work on Continental politics, always immaculate).
- Chef **Felicien**; **Georges** (ex-English Embassy Paris).
- Fjord talk: Maas to Duchess ("Providence... pleasing the British tourist"); Duchess hates tourists; Foote on dhobie's "three annas", proposes university at Vienna; Foote's Paris boot-pitching neighbour (Dobson's countryman).
- Browne's walk: Browne goes ashore with party; Miss Verney and Browne bring up rear. Browne leaves party to send boat back; mist descends.
- Browne hears woman's cry, "Help me," in English (Russian accent). Found clinging to **birch tree** on hillside near precipice. She: **Katherine Petrovitch**. She was painting on mountain; fell.
- Browne lowers coat by sleeve; hauls her up. Carries her about a mile to mountain road. Sends a boy to hotel.
- Arrives: **Madame Bernstein** (stout, elderly, guardian), cabriole with shaggy pony, led by villager. Katherine: "Permit me to introduce you to my guardian."
- Browne's name: "I am Browne's Mimosa Soap, Fragrant and Antiseptic."

### Ch II
- Yacht: guests cross-examine Browne. He gives half-truth (lost in fog).
- Foote's anecdote: Rigi with **Simeon Baynes** (American millionaire) and daughter (married Italian count who fought Constantovitch, killed in Abyssinia).
- Dinner poor (Duke commanded to Osborne; Miss Verney sulks).
- Browne & Maas at rail: Schiller quote "Leben heisst traeumen; weise sein heisst angenehm traeumen." Browne rants on marriage market; Maas cites Ben Jonson.
- Maas's plans: fortnight with Duchess in Midlands, Paris, south, Cairo.
- Browne talks of Russia; mentions **Demetrovitch** (handsome, enormous moustache, stayed at Newmarket; ordered by Czar to estates). Maas smiles.
- Next morning Browne goes ashore (confer with local authority). Maas tags along, walks up mountain road.
- Browne visits Madame Bernstein at hotel (she thanks him in French, "Mon Dieu!"). Maas found in hotel room with Vermouth.
- Yacht leaves for Aalsund; passes Pulpit Rock.

### Ch III
- Six months later, first week of March. Browne in Monolith Club, Pall Mall. Travels since: Russia (bears with Demetrovitch), Crimea, Constantinople, Cairo, dahabiyeh to Luxor (French countess, Austrian archduke, German diplomat), Monte Carlo, Paris.
- Foote arrives. Browne proposes Algiers; will wire **Mason** (skipper) to have yacht ready at Plymouth.
- Walk up Regent Street; picture-shop near Charles Street crossing (Waterloo Place). Water-colour of Merok by Katherine.
- Shopman: she visited that morning; selling work; "in a hurry to sell". Address card: **Miss KATHERINE PETROVITCH, 43, German Park Road, West.** Browne forbids shopman to tell her his name.
- Browne in hansom: "Cabby, drive me to 43, German Park Road." Foote: "John Grantham Browne... lunatic asylum." Foote to Jermyn Street rooms; "Algiers will not have the pleasure of entertaining me."

### Ch IV
- Melbury Road; fog; Browne gives cabman half-sovereign ("Put it into the first charity-box").
- No. 43: studio, side door. Katherine doesn't recognise him at first.
- Tea "a la Russe" (samovar, lemon). She: family "dangerous persons", prohibited in Russia. Studio lent by an English woman artist met in Berlin, who winters in Venice. She and Madame lodge in **Warwick Road**.
- Browne invites them to theatre/opera; **Lohengrin** at Covent Garden. Plans dinner at **Lallemand's**.
- Browne's thought: "He shall sit beside Madame Bernstein."

### Ch V
- Restaurateur **Alphonse** (Lallemand's, "No. 6" room). Browne orders best dinner.
- Foote at **Welter Club** playing black pool with **Bellingham of the Blues**. Foote guesses Browne's love ("put two and two together"; "gooseberry"; "Lohengrin... dose of Wagner").
- Browne in love. Katherine's note accepting, midday post; scent. Miss Verney's letters noted as less dear.

### Ch VI
- Lallemand's dinner. Madame Bernstein in ruby velvet, bare arms, false diamonds. Katherine in black, velvet band at throat. Madame claims to have known Garibaldi and Kossuth.
- Katherine: "Music and painting are my two greatest pleasures."
- Covent Garden box (prompt side); Lohengrin. Foote draws Madame aside.
- Browne asks Katherine to meet; she evades ("I do not know what Madame Bernstein's arrangements are").
- Foote: Perigord Club supper. Browne to walk home.
- Next morning: Kensington Gardens; German Park Road studio; old woman with yellow soap; Browne tips 5 shillings.
- High Street: meets Katherine. Declares love ("I have no desire save to make you happy"). Gate: she says "Good-bye, Mr. Browne," tears.
- Next day 11 am: studio no answer; Warwick Road: maid says she and Madame left for Paris this morning.

### Ch VII
- Maid (landlady **Mrs. Jimson**, servant **Jane**): left at nine, "I leave for Paris in an hour's time." Katherine had been crying; quarrel with Madame.
- Madame's Paris address on slip: **"Madame Bernstein, 35, Rue Jacquarie, Paris."**
- Browne catches 11 o'clock Charing Cross express via Dover–Calais. Valet; coachman **Williams**.
- Paris hotel (his usual, **Place Vendome**). Fiacre to Rue Jacquarie; watches house; two people look alarmed at him.
- "Drive me to the Amphitryon Club."

### Ch VIII
- **Amphitryon Club**, Avenue de l'Opera. Maas there: thought Browne in St. Petersburg. Rumour (from **Deauville**) of Browne's marriage; Browne denies.
- Maas to self: "Our friend Browne is bent upon making a fool of himself."
- Next morning: Browne meets Katherine on boulevard. Walk to Tuileries (Omphale by Eude; Aeneas statue). She: annoyed he followed her. Browne: "I cannot tell you how..." She: "If you will promise not to repeat the offence." He promises not to follow her. She promises to write if she leaves Paris (he gives address).
- Madame's letter, pink paper, very scented, signed **"SOPHIE BERNSTEIN"**: asks him to call Thursday afternoon.

### Ch IX
- Madame's sitting-room (Rue Jacquarie). Madame says Katherine loves Browne; asks him to go away. Browne: "I do love her."
- Katherine enters; Madame's cover story: "discussion on modern French art."
- Browne declares love in full; Katherine: "I do love you"; he kisses her; "my affianced lover."
- Madame: "my work in life is done." Browne proposes Fontainebleau tomorrow. Dinner Maison Doree at eight.

### Ch X
- Browne buys plain heavy gold ring at jeweller's.
- Dinner: Madame, Katherine, Browne (Browne's wedding dinner).
- Fontainebleau trip: train via Yeres valley, Melun. Palace (Napoleon's rooms, Marie Antoinette, Francis I, King of Rome's cradle, abdication table); carp, labyrinth, vineries; forest; dinner at Hotel de France et d'Angleterre. Katherine made him chocolate on the morning.
- On return train Browne puts ring on Katherine's finger: "The symbol of my love, darling."
- Returns Katherine to Madame before 9 pm.
- Next morning: letter from Katherine: "When you asked me... to be your wife... no other man shall ever call me wife.--KATHERINE PETROVITCH."

### Ch XI
- Rue Jacquarie: Madame with smelling-salts, claims quarrel with Katherine over Browne.
- Louvre, Room IV: Titian's "Entombment of Christ." Katherine there. Browne: "your husband in the sight of God, if not by the law of man."
- Gallery corner; Browne: "Tell me everything."

### Ch XII
- Katherine's story:
  - Real name **Polowski**; Petrovitch is mother's maiden name.
  - Born **Warsaw**. Mother Hungarian, beautiful singer; died when Katherine was 7.
  - Old servant **Maritza**. Father arrested as Nihilist; part of plot to kill the Czar; sent to Siberia (penal servitude for life). Later drafted to **island of Saghalien**.
  - **Madame Bernstein** = old friend of father's; adopted Katherine.
  - Inheritance from mother's brother: £300/yr; Madame manages.
  - Father now ill, dying; news via Madame.
  - Katherine plans to rescue father. Browne offers help on condition: she becomes his wife once done. Bargain struck; she kisses him.
- Browne plans to tell Madame nothing of help beyond what's needed.
- Browne at Amphitryon: meets Maas (Vellencourt married). Browne says he wants yachting trip to Farther East. Maas: "Madame Bernstein, her adopted daughter, and the islands north of Japan."

### Ch XIII
- Narrator reflection on fate.
- Katherine's note: "To-night an old friend... Herr Otto Sauber... knew my father."
- Madame's room, that evening: Sauber (small, round face, wrinkled, white curly hair, seventy-ish, threadbare). Sauber weeps. Madame plans escape in detail (knows Russian prisons, governors).

### Ch XIV
- Sauber walks with Browne to Rue Auber corner: "you know absolutely nothing." Warns against Madame ("tongue runs riot"; her husband's old friend). Gives address of **Johann Schmidt**, Hong-kong (specialist; New Caledonia). Will write letter.
- Browne and Katherine at Tuileries next morning. Browne warns her against Madame. She defends Madame; he promises not to tell Katherine what he plans beyond what Madame can know. Browne leaves for London that afternoon.
- Calais boat: Maas.

### Ch XV
- Maas on board; Browne tells him of engagement; "She will not go out with me."
- Dover; Charing Cross; Maas.
- Browne at home; painting of Merok in gallery (Waterloo / Park Lane).
- Lawyer **Bretherton** (Chancery Lane): Browne makes Katherine heir of most of his fortune (will). Browne explains dangerous work.
- Captain **Mason** (short, stout, red face, fringe beard, Browne's father's skipper).

### Ch XVI
- Mason: ready Monday next. Told: Japan; keep secret; "Peculiar errand." Crew to be good men; Browne asks about seas north of Japan (Yesso, Gulf of Tartary).
- **Foote** at Monolith; Green Park. Browne tells Foote everything. Foote: "I am coming with you, happen what may." Note: "Dear old man, I am coming with you, happen what may.--Always your friend, J. FOOTE."

### Ch XVII
- Maas meets Browne in Park Lane: doctor says he must leave England (lungs). Asks to join voyage. Browne reluctant but invites him. Sail Monday from Southampton.
- Browne pushes Maas off; Foote in Pall Mall. Foote says Maas hypochondriac (claims). Foote: don't tell Maas. Browne to Paris (Katherine & Madame to leave for Japan in a French boat in two days).

### Ch XVIII
- Paris Rue Jacquarie: Katherine embraces Browne. Browne buys her dressing-bag and sables in Rue de la Paix.
- Train from Paris 2:15 pm to Marseilles. Special saloon. Stop at Laroche, Dijon, Pontanevaux.
- Browne's dreams: Merok cliff; Maas pulls to kill Katherine; Japan garden bridge.
- Marseilles; steamer; Katherine embarks for East; Browne leaves ship.

### Ch XIX
- Train back; Foote meets at Dover. Foote: Mason ready; sail Monday.
- Browne & Foote to London; 50 invitations declined.
- Foote: marriage out of circle; Miss Verney "forgotten" (Browne winces).
- Ring talisman: "while he wore it, he could come to no harm."
- Southampton; Lotus Blossom at Royal Pier. Sail Sunday/Monday; Swanage; Old Harry.
- Breakfast banter (Maas/Foote, pâté, air-bottling, matrimonial registry). Maas: "a scheme for helping long-sentenced burglars escape."

### Ch XX
- Maas's remark makes them pale. Foote: "unintentional bull's-eye."
- Plymouth, Gibraltar (Officers' Mess; Bramthwaite of 43rd Midlandshire).
- Maas: Browne's "fiancée" name — Maas claims a friend, Miss Corniquet, French artist, knows Katherine.
- Port Said, Suez, Aden, Colombo, Singapore, Hong-kong (Ly-ee-moon Pass, Green Island, Victoria harbour).
- Club; Browne presents letter from **George Pellister**. Host (unnamed) gives address of Johann Schmidt. Host warns Schmidt bad reputation. Browne invites host to dine.

### Ch XXI
- Schmidt's shop, Chinese characters + "Johann Schmidt." Chinese shopkeeper.
- Schmidt: big German, pipe, flannel shirt, black alpaca coat. Says he doesn't know Sauber. Office behind curtain (Cantonese dragon chair). Reads Sauber's letter; "I do remember Herr Sauber."
- Browne reveals plan; Schmidt: "Dis a very strange work"; will find a man; will "communicate mit you before ten o'clock to-night." Asks where yacht anchored (suspicious).

### Ch XXII
- Dinner aboard with host (unnamed). Maas quiet; slipped away earlier to telegraph station (learned months later from Foote).
- **MacAndrew** (tall, slim, white clothes, helmet, educated drawl) comes aboard by sampan. Plan on note: £5,000 in solid gold, paid first. Browne: "I will let you know my decision then."
- Browne burns note. Maas's cigar-case "lost". Browne finds the envelope gone in cabin.

### Ch XXIII
- Browne's night; valet Davis denies. Dawn: MacAndrew by sampan. Two wooden gold boxes (£5,000). Meeting "13th". MacAndrew sails out.
- Yokohama (Fujiyama seen; Thursday). Katherine at Club Hotel verandah; Browne tells her of MacAndrew plan. Madame: "another fortnight."

### Ch XXIV
- Fortnight in Japan. Katherine on yacht; "some day this vessel will be your own."
- Maas asks to join party; Browne consents reluctantly; Foote disapproves.
- Maas reveals he knows: Nihilist; Polowski. Learned from friend ("daughter of the famous Polowski"). Offers help; will land on island.
- Foote distrusts Maas ("lay a hundred pounds to a halfpenny"). Maas softens later.
- Cape Siretoko (Saghalien's southernmost point), fourteen days after Yokohama.

### Ch XXV
- Three weeks later: Browne in small log-hut, north side of **Bay of Kroptskoi**, awaiting fugitive. Settlement of six huts, once coal-mine track to **Dui**. Forest (taiga). Full moon; ice-chinking.
- Fog; Browne reads Miss Braddon novel bought at Dover; dozes.
- MacAndrew arrives at night with tall gray-bearded man carrying the convict. Convict: short, bullet head half-shaven, red hair, querulous, suspicious. Browne disappointed.
- MacAndrew: disguised as Russian fur merchant; reached Dui; "hasn't the heart of a louse."
- Convict called "Monsieur Petrovitch"; asks "You are... my Katherine's affianced husband?"

### Ch XXVI
- Waiting for yacht; signal at midnight from hut (rocket). Yacht signals back. Boat from yacht (third mate **Phillips**).
- Convict dressed; speaks in French: "My dear daughter... When last I saw her she was but a little child."
- Hut left burning; wolves; boat; convict lifted aboard.
- Yacht deck-house meeting: Katherine & father; Madame recognises him ("Stefan," she sobs).
- Maas urges staying until morning; captain Mason agrees (strong current, fog). Browne consents.
- Katherine uneasy; sleeps. Dawn: captain reports engine breakdown; second officer reports Russian man-o'-war.

### Ch XXVII
- Smoking-room council: Browne, MacAndrew, Maas, Foote, captain Mason, chief-engineer **M'Cartney**. Main crosshead-pin removed; duplicates also taken.
- Hiding place: tunnel of tail-shaft (MacAndrew and convict). Katherine told; Browne tells her father will be hidden.
- Katherine: "what will become of my poor father?" Browne reassures.
- Foote: "come up to the smoking-room"; Maas caught.

### Ch XXVIII
- Second engineer confesses: Maas bribed him (£500 offered; refused). Maas claimed Browne would run yacht into a trap.
- Maas protests; MacAndrew forces him (revolver; "Mr. Browne, take his legs"). MacAndrew uses Browne's medicine-chest (dark fluid, sedative). Maas drinks, sleeps, "pneumonia" cover story. Foote nurses.
- Hail: boat from cruiser coming alongside.

### Ch XXIX
- Foote watches Maas. Russian officer (tall, ~30) boards; asks to overhaul yacht; Browne protests.
- Search: men's quarters, engine-room (convict cough near the tunnel), smoking-room, deck-house, drawing-room, Maas's cabin (Foote as doctor; officer satisfied not the man), Katherine's and Browne's cabins.
- Officer: fugitive is **"Kleinkopf"**, "most expert diamond-thief in Europe." Not a Nihilist.
- Madame faints in drawing-room; Browne carries her to cabin.
- Cruiser leaves. Captain: engine repaired. Browne unsettled: Madame's recognition vs. "Kleinkopf."
- Browne tells Foote; Foote: "I'll find out... private inquiry agent."

### Ch XXX
- Katherine at taffrail: asks Browne to give up marrying her and put her ashore. Browne refuses.
- Foote & MacAndrew reveal: convict = **the Red Rat**; a diamond thief; **Madame Bernstein's husband**. Real Petrovitch/Polowski died early last year on Saghalien (MacAndrew: "He is dead. He died early last year.").
- Browne tells Katherine everything; she goes to cabin.
- Brig sighted SW; boat from brig; MacAndrew.
- Maas landed at **Tomari, Kunashiri** (in Kuriles) by brig, three months' time.
- Browne gives MacAndrew envelope of money for Madame & Maas. MacAndrew: "You have helped me amazingly."
- Hakodate; Browne's plan: wedding in Yokohama, Foote best man.
- Final: moon; "The first is that we are together, and the second is that you are not THE RED RAT'S DAUGHTER!" END.

## BOOK 2: TOMMY (Joseph Hocking, 1916, Hodder & Stoughton)
- Note by author: based on real soldiers; Hocking addressed recruiting meetings; visited France/Flanders; La Bassee, Neuve Chapelle, Ypres. Dated Priors' Corner, Totteridge, Herts, Feb 1916.

### Ch I
- **Tom Pollard** (~23), lives Dixon Street, Brunford (Lancashire mill town). Parents Ezekiel (weaver, 30s/week) and **Martha Pollard** (ex-weaver; blunt speech).
- Sunday, first in June 1914. Tom to **Thorn and Thistle** pub. Brunford Town Hall clock.
- **Polly Powell** (~24, buxom, bold-eyed, red cheeks, black eyes, highly coloured dress; daughter of landlord **Enoch Powell**). Jealous; wants Tom. Mentions **Jim Scott**, **Jim Dixon**.
- Polly: father says Tom has brains; Tom took three prizes at Mechanics' Institute. Tom promised Tackler's job.
- **Alice Lister** (~20, refined, contralto, pianist; father **George Lister**, small manufacturer; mother **Mrs. Lister**). Walk in Liverpool Road / Scott's Park.
- Alice: Tom must choose: her or the Thorn and Thistle. Tom: "I'm noan going to be a Methody parson." Walks off, goes with **Harry Waterman** to the **Rose and Crown** club.
- Waterman: tall, handsome, florid, light-brown hair; claims squire's son from Warwickshire; trained in cotton; studied in German universities; laughed Tom out of Young Men's Class.
- Tom goes back to Polly; drunk that night. Mother: "Thou'st gi'en up a nice lass for a brazen-faaced 'uzzy."

### Ch II
- Brunford boom; Tom neglects studies, drinks at Thorn and Thistle. Rumours of war (Austria–Serbia). Manufacturers' talk about Germans. August 1914: England enters war. Powell: "six weeks."
- **Mr. Shweitzer**, German businessman, dinner at Bull and Butcher hotel: says Wilhelm II will be "your future king." Englishman punches him; jaw broken.
- Tom holds back from enlisting; Polly discourages. Elijah Butterworth (three sons in army) scolds Tom.
- New Year 1915: recruiting meeting at Mechanics' Institute. Speaker (who had been in Belgium) rouses hall. Tom: "No! By God, no!" walks to platform, gives name. "Thus Tom became a soldier."
- Mother: "Ay, tha mun be sent to Lancaster asylum."

### Ch III
- Tom tells Polly; she: "if you have done it, what do you want to speak to me about it for?" Asks if he might be an officer. Polly promises to be true.
- Alice meets Tom at Town Hall; praises him; "we shall be praying for you." Tom: "young parson going after you?"
- Joins Loyal North Lancashires (not named battalion). Drill; grows taller/fitter; discipline problems (drunk and disorderly; punished).
- **Robert Penrose** (Cornish, Charterhouse-educated, private, refused commission, later Lieutenant) — chides Tom; attends Y.M.C.A.; French class with a Frenchman.
- **Alec McPhail** (Scottish, Black Watch; whisky; Colonel Ingersoll; mother a godly Scotswoman). Tom and McPhail walk; Tom returns to pub.
- Colonel's punishment: "Why did you make a beast of yourself?" Tom sent to Y.M.C.A.
- Penrose: "You'll end by being kicked out of the Army." Tom goes to Y.M.C.A. hall; French verbs ("Je suis... Vous etes...").
- Leave in Brunford: Tom drinks with Polly; Alice avoided.
- Battalion moves to Surrey camp (May). Waterloo; Penrose's old school Charterhouse near Godalming.
- Camp: Y.M.C.A. huts. Tom meets **Lieutenant Waterman** there; Waterman recognises him.

### Ch IV
- Narrator: Tom's camp life; Tom tells him about French, Y.M.C.A.
- Mother's letter: Polly walking out with Jim Dixon; "sack her."
- Alec McPhail drinks; Tom rebukes; Alec confesses fear, whisky as courage. Battalion ordered to France.
- Farewell meeting at Y.M.C.A.: special speaker; "Jesus Christ... Captain, Guide, Saviour." Alec makes decision for God; leaves canteen.
- Folkestone, Boulogne, troop train, march; guns booming; "Look at yon' airship".

### Ch V
- Ypres salient. Sergeant (Ashworth) describes 1914 battles, Cloth Hall, Cathedral; German poison gas; sergeant hates shirkers.
- Ruined Ypres; Tom in front trenches; **Lancashire lad** shot through head looking over sandbags.
- Fourth trip: bombardment; bayonet fight. Young officer goes to rescue wounded German who shoots him; German hands; narrator notes.
- Tom's companions: heroism of humdrum men. Waterman as staff officer passes Tom.
- Night sentry duty: German silence; Tom prays aloud "O God!" repeatedly; comforted.

### Ch VI
- Alice Lister: Tom's leaving; refused parson **Mr. Skelton**.
- **Harry Briarfield** (24, partner in father's business; Sunday school teacher; proposes). Alice asks for 3 days.
- Parents: George and Mrs. Lister. Alice doesn't answer. At midnight, prays: "O God, save him!" Same time as Tom's prayer.

### Ch VII
- German sentry shouts across: Lancashires to attack 6 am. Tom reports to subaltern; Black Watch brought up; attack repelled.
- Colonel (also "Major Blundell") questions Tom; Sergeant Ashworth praises Tom.
- Tom's conversion: "God was a personal Power ever present with him."
- Alec McPhail wounded; Tom visits hospital (road to Cassel). Nurse. Alec: "I gave my life to the Lord." Tom and Alec sing "Jesu, Lover of my soul" and recite Psalm 23 together. Alec dies next day: "It's a' richt."

### Ch VIII
- **Colonel Blount** and **Major Blundell**; General Withers (Divisional HQ). Leaks of plans; "an Achan in the camp."
- Tom sees Waterman with Blundell; suspicious. Captain Winfield (battalion).
- Tom sees Waterman at night, throws white paper over sandbags toward German lines. Tom attacks him. Penrose (now Lieutenant) intervenes. Major Blundell arrives.
- Tom crosses no-man's-land (~100 yards); German takes paper; Tom fights, breaks German's shoulder blade (football trick); takes paper; shot in left arm and right shoulder.
- Colonel Blount visits Tom; will make Waterman answer.

### Ch IX
- Court; Tom's evidence. Waterman admits: German at heart, "I have counted the cost." Parents spelled name with two n's (Waterman's real name possibly German). Court: Waterman shot at wall, stands erect.
- Tom to be recommended for D.C.M.

### Ch X
- Newspapers: "Heroism of a Lancashire Lad." Mrs. Pollard's comments. Tom recommended for D.C.M.
- Tom home on leave (Dec). Left London King's Cross 10 am. Thinks of Alice; learns Mrs. Pollard wrote Alice was not engaged... (later confirmed: Alice never engaged to Harry).
- Home crowd: Polly at station; Tom snubs her ("I don't want to play gooseberry"); declares teetotal.
- Parents kneel and pray together.

### Ch XI
- Tom wakes (Sunday, quarter to twelve). Church that night with parents. Meets Alice in vestibule. "How are you, Alice?" Walks her home.
- Alice: never engaged to Harry Briarfield; never to parson. Tom asks her to wait till war ends; she agrees.
- George Lister to wife: "our Alice is a fool" / Mrs. Lister: "yon's a grand lad."
- Tom's leave ends; George Lister and Alice see Tom off at Waterloo. Tom: "au revoir." Alice: "loving you all the time." Tom: "God help me to do my bit, and then take me back to her."
- Narrator's closing: Tom will fight on.

## KEY NAMES INDEX (quick)
- Book 1: Browne; Foote; Maas; Katherine (Petrovitch/Polowski); Madame Sophie Bernstein; Herr Otto Sauber; Johann Schmidt; MacAndrew; Mason; Bretherton; Demetrovitch; Stefan (convict, Red Rat / Kleinkopf); M'Cartney; Phillips; Miss Verney; Duchess of Matlock; Lallemand; Alphonse; Felicien; Davis (valet); Williams (coachman); Jane & Mrs. Jimson; Maritza; Lord Rushbrooke; old Brown.
- Book 2: Tom Pollard; Martha & Ezekiel Pollard; Polly Powell; Enoch Powell; Alice Lister; George & Mrs. Lister; Harry Waterman; Harry Briarfield; Robert Penrose; Alec McPhail; Sergeant Ashworth; Colonel Blount; Major Blundell; General Withers; Captain Winfield; Mr. Shweitzer; Elijah Butterworth; Mr. Skelton; Nick; Jim Dixon; Jim Scott; Emily Bilson; Jim Parkin.
